39:#### Previous Task Filters
46:#### Chained Tasks
#### Previous Task Filters

The filters are one dropdown, never a bar of chips: a small ghost button with a filter icon at the right of the Previous group's heading in the Tasks tab, shown while the group holds a task, reading "Filter", or, while any filter is on, how many are, as "Filter · 2", in the theme's accent. Clicking it opens a menu beneath it, one column, never wider than the sidebar, holding two sections, each headed by a small muted label, "Mode" and "Other mode", their options one per line, each with a checkbox, and the menu stays open while options are checked, closing on a click outside it or <Escape>. Each option reads its label and, muted after it, how many previous tasks match it on its own, whatever other options are checked; the latest task, heading the view, is never counted.
The Mode section filters by the mode each task was sent in, one option per task mode in the [PromptModesScope](./modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope)'s order, "Code", "Chain", "Spec", and "Freeform", each with a small dot in its mode's colour before its label. The Other mode section filters by where a task stands with the other mode, as the [PromptSendingScope](./sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) says, with "Can send to Spec" for tasks that offer Send to Spec, "Can send to Code" for those that offer Send to Code, "Sent" for those already sent to the other mode or being sent there, and "Marked done" for those marked done by hand.
With no option checked, which is how the list starts, every previous task shows. Within a section, the options checked combine as either, so a task shows when it matches any of them, and the two sections combine as both, so with options checked in each, a task shows only when it matches one in each. Clicking an option checks or unchecks it, the list filtering at once behind the open menu, and a "Clear filters" line at the menu's foot, shown only while any option is checked, unchecks them all. An option that would show no tasks is still listed, its count 0, and can still be checked.
Filtering only hides tasks from the list; it changes nothing about them. A chain whose steps are hidden in part keeps its parent row above the steps still shown, and is hidden with its parent only when none of its steps shows. Session dividers show only above a session with a task shown. The row's count still counts every previous task, and while any option is checked, the Previous group's heading, after its count, reads " · N shown", N counting the previous tasks the filters show. A hidden task stays selected if it was, and is still counted in "N selected" and sent by the batch actions; an open task that is filtered out closes. With every task filtered out, the list reads "No previous tasks match these filters", muted, centred. The filters are kept while the list is closed and opened again, and each open project keeps its own, as the [OpenProjectsScope](../open-projects/index.md#open-projects-scope) says, but they are not saved with the project.

content.text:
The previous-task filters are now one dropdown instead of the bar of chips. All tests pass (565, 1 ignored) and clippy shows no new warnings.

- **Button:** a small "Filter" button with a funnel icon sits at the right of the Previous heading whenever there's a task to filter. While filters are on, it reads "Filter · N" in the accent colour.
- **Menu:** clicking the button opens a single-column menu below it, no wider than the sidebar, with two sections:
  - "Mode": Code, Chain, Spec and Freeform, each with a dot in its mode's colour.
  - "Other mode": Can send to Spec, Can send to Code, Sent and Marked done.
  - Each option has a checkbox, its label, and its match count in muted text.
- **Behaviour:** checking an option filters the list straight away while the menu stays open. "Clear filters" appears at the bottom while any filter is on. The menu closes on a click outside it or Escape.
- **Unchanged:** the filtering rules, the " · N shown" count and selected-but-hidden tasks work as before.

The menu is drawn over the whole Tasks tab rather than inside the heading row, so the 28px row doesn't clip it and it stays put when the list scrolls. With the filter bar gone, the list has one fewer row.

I updated the filter test to open the menu, check an option and confirm the menu stays open, then clear and close it. Escape is tested by sending the window's Escape action directly, because the test window doesn't bind the key itself.

The spec and the prompt don't disagree here.
